questions.stem: Which graph represents a complete graph with 4 vertices?
questions.solution: A complete graph has an edge between every pair of vertices. In this case, graph A has edges connecting all pairs of vertices (0-1, 0-2, 0-3, 1-2, 1-3, and 2-3), satisfying the definition of a complete graph with 4 vertices.
questions.explanation: A complete graph must have an edge between every pair of vertices. Graph B is missing an edge (2-3), graph C is missing two edges (2-3 and 0-3), and graph D has a weighted edge which does not affect connectivity but might confuse the reader about the definition of a complete graph.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B or C because they lack an edge connecting two vertices. Remember that all pairs of vertices must be connected in a complete graph.

questions.stem: Identify which graph represents a complete graph with 5 vertices.
questions.solution: Graph A represents a complete graph with 5 vertices because it has an edge connecting every pair of vertices (0-1, 0-2, 0-3, 0-4, 1-2, 1-3, 1-4, 2-3, 2-4, and 3-4).
questions.explanation: A complete graph must have an edge between every pair of vertices. Graph B is missing two edges (3-4 and 2-4), graph C is missing one edge (2-4), and graph D has a weighted edge which does not affect connectivity but might confuse the reader about the definition of a complete graph.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B, C, or D because they lack an edge connecting two vertices or include extra edges. Remember that a complete graph must connect every pair of vertices.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a complete graph?
questions.solution: Graph A is not a complete graph because it lacks an edge connecting vertex 1 and vertex 2.
questions.explanation: A complete graph must have an edge between every pair of vertices. Graph A only has edges (0-1, 0-2, and 1-2), missing the connection between vertex 1 and vertex 2. The other options represent graphs with connections between all pairs of vertices.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B, C, or D because they have multiple edges or additional vertices. Remember that a complete graph must connect every pair of vertices, regardless of the number of edges or extra vertices.

questions.stem: Which graph represents a complete graph with 3 vertices?
questions.solution: Graph A represents a complete graph with 3 vertices because it has an edge connecting vertex 0 and vertex 1, vertex 0 and vertex 2, and vertex 1 and vertex 2.
questions.explanation: A complete graph must have an edge between every pair of vertices. Graph B is missing an edge (2-3), graph C includes an extra edge (1-3) that is not required for a complete graph with only 3 vertices, and graph D has a weighted edge which does not affect connectivity but might confuse the reader about the definition of a complete graph.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B or C because they lack an edge connecting two vertices or include extra edges. Remember that all pairs of vertices must be connected in a complete graph, and the number of vertices determines the required connections.

questions.stem: Identify which graph is NOT a complete graph with 6 vertices.
questions.solution: Graph D is NOT a complete graph with 6 vertices because it lacks edges between vertex 4 and vertex 5, and vertex 3 and vertex 5.
questions.explanation: A complete graph must have an edge between every pair of vertices. Graphs A, B, and C are missing edges required for a complete graph with 6 vertices (B misses an edge between vertex 4 and vertex 5, C misses an edge between vertex 4 and vertex 5, and D misses two edges: 4-5 and 3-5).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A because it seems to have too many edges. Remember that the question asks for a graph NOT representing a complete graph, and graphs B, C, and D are missing required connections.
